capabilities: Mirror the Zotero library as one JSON file per item plus per-PDF annotation files
Sync incrementally via Zotero's local HTTP API with deletion reconcile
Generate per-item note views from custom templates
Write Dataview dashboard notes for items, PDFs, annotations and stats
Fuzzy-search the mirror and insert reference cards into notes
disambiguation: Not a one-off citation importer; it keeps a complete live mirror of the Zotero library as JSON files in the vault.
extras: Install instructions describe a development build (npm install && npm run build). Sync only runs while Obsidian is open; edits made in Zotero arrive on the next poll, window focus, or startup. The README documents detailed troubleshooting for Zotero's minimal HTTP server and legacy zotero://select links.
intentEvidence: This is the difference between an import plugin and a Zotero client inside Obsidian.
motivation: The author wanted library data as a queryable, git-versionable mirror that stays available offline, instead of one-off imported markdown snapshots that drift from Zotero.
problem: Import-style Zotero plugins produce static, template-bound snapshots that age and require Zotero to be open, leaving no live, queryable copy of the library in the vault.

relations.evidence: Zotero ships a local HTTP API (Settings → Advanced → "Allow other applications on this computer to communicate with Zotero")
Dataview, Templater, scripts or your own plugins can load any of these files

requires.name: Zotero 7+ desktop app for local API sync
zotero.org API key for the optional Web API source
zotero.org account for the Web API source
Dataview, for the generated dashboard notes

summary: Mirrors a Zotero library into a git-versioned JSON folder in the vault, syncing incrementally over Zotero's local HTTP API and generating queryable note views.
